open_points.subject: sign-in throttling state
open_points.text: “A successful sign-in clears the count” and “a restart clears them” conflict with `refused_sign_ins(last 15min) >= 5 => sign_in refused`, which contains neither reset.
open_points.question: After a successful sign-in or restart, do refusals that occurred within the previous 15 minutes still cause lockout?
options: Use a resettable in-memory counter, so earlier refusals no longer count
Use the rolling 15-minute refusal history despite a success or restart
open_points.default_guess: Use the resettable in-memory counter described by the normative rules.

open_points.subject: owner-session cookie
open_points.text: “carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin”
open_points.question: What exact cookie scope, SameSite policy, Secure behavior, path and treatment of loopback HTTP enforce these requirements?
options: Permit a non-Secure cookie only on loopback and use a host-only, HttpOnly, SameSite cookie
Require HTTPS and a Secure cookie everywhere
Apply different cookies or policies to local and remote access
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, Secure except for explicitly recognized loopback HTTP.

open_points.subject: CSRF on sign-in
open_points.text: “Every change in the owner interface carries the CSRF protection bound to its session”
open_points.question: Is sign-in exempt from CSRF checking because no owner session exists yet, or must it have a separate pre-authentication CSRF mechanism?
options: Sign-in is exempt; CSRF begins after session creation
Sign-in uses a separate pre-authentication CSRF value
Sign-in requires an existing anonymous session carrying CSRF state
open_points.default_guess: Treat sign-in as exempt from session-bound CSRF and apply CSRF to changes after authentication.

open_points.subject: confirmation input binding
open_points.text: “kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order”
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm, value encoding, field order and normalization define equality between the shown inputs and the submitted inputs?
options: Specify a canonical byte serialization and cryptographic digest
Store and compare the structured values directly
Leave serialization and digest selection to each implementation
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned canonical serialization and a cryptographic digest fixed by the specification.

open_points.subject: import mapping contents
open_points.text: “answers ... each project the file holds with its id and status” and, for picks, “their rooms and pointers; the display name and alias ... [and] the Customers the import will make”
open_points.question: Must the mapping also show every other imported project fact, especially the object address, kind, characteristics, customer link, revisions and carried instants, before confirmation?
options: Show every fact that the transaction will store
Show only the facts expressly enumerated
Show only transformed or conflicting facts, leaving copied facts implicit
open_points.default_guess: Show every fact that will be stored for each picked project and its related records.

open_points.subject: duplicate project ids outside the picks
open_points.text: Rule 3 says records only of unpicked projects “take no part in the duplicate-id check”, but also says a file that “holds two project records with one id ... is refused whole at upload, before anything is picked.”
open_points.question: Does a duplicate project id anywhere in the file refuse upload, or are duplicate ids ignored when all affected projects are ultimately unpicked?
options: Refuse every file containing duplicate project ids at upload
Defer duplicate checking until picks exist and check picked records only
Check project-id duplicates globally but nested-record duplicates only within picks
open_points.default_guess: Refuse duplicate project ids globally at upload because project selection would otherwise be ambiguous.

open_points.subject: import file identity
open_points.text: “The mapping names the file by its digest” and `closure.file_digest = digest(f)`
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm and exact byte representation identify an uploaded file, and is that identity versioned so later releases reproduce it?
options: Digest the exact uploaded bytes with a specified, versioned algorithm
Digest a canonical parsed representation
Let each release choose its digest representation
open_points.default_guess: Digest the exact uploaded bytes with a cryptographic algorithm fixed and versioned by the specification.

open_points.subject: missing configured store
open_points.text: A17 says that when the configured store file does not exist Registry “makes a new, empty store”, while R0-89 and A18 say that when the store is lost the owner restores the newest kept backup.
open_points.question: How does startup distinguish a deliberate first installation from accidental store loss, and may it silently create an empty production store when backups or prior state exist?
options: Require an explicit initialization mode before creating an empty store
Always create an empty store whenever the file is absent
Refuse creation when the backup location indicates prior backups, but create otherwise
open_points.default_guess: Require explicit initialization; otherwise refuse startup when the configured store is absent.

open_points.subject: configuration item namespace
open_points.text: “The configuration holds exactly these items and no other” and “an ... unknown item fails the start.”
open_points.question: Which source or namespace is considered Registry configuration for detecting unknown items, rather than unrelated process environment or deployment settings?
options: A dedicated configuration file or environment-variable prefix
The entire process environment
Only recognized keys are read and unrelated keys are ignored
open_points.default_guess: Use a dedicated Registry namespace and reject unknown items only within it.

open_points.subject: secret length and equality
open_points.text: “A secret ... is at least 32 bytes long” and “No two secrets are equal.”
open_points.question: Are length and equality checked on configured text bytes, decoded secret bytes, or a normalized representation, and which encodings are valid?
options: Require a specified encoding and compare decoded bytes
Compare the exact configured UTF-8 bytes
Treat secrets as opaque strings and count characters
open_points.default_guess: Specify one encoding and perform length and equality checks on the decoded secret bytes.

open_points.subject: backup encryption format
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” and “A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.”
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce generation, key format, metadata authentication and key-digest algorithm define a valid encrypted backup?
options: Specify a versioned authenticated-encryption container
Rely on an implementation-selected encryption library and format
Encrypt only the store payload while leaving unauthenticated metadata outside
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned authenticated-encryption container whose metadata is authenticated and whose algorithms are fixed by the specification.

open_points.subject: restore with no usable kept backup
open_points.text: “the owner restores the newest kept backup” but a failed run still deletes backups older than 30 days, and backups are checked only when made.
open_points.question: What happens when no kept backup exists, or when the newest kept backup has become unreadable or corrupt since its creation?
options: Try older kept backups newest-first
Stop recovery and require an external copy
Create a new empty store
Retain at least one verified backup regardless of age
open_points.default_guess: Try older kept backups newest-first and refuse to start a replacement store if none verifies.

open_points.subject: backup status with no kept backup
open_points.text: “the owner interface shows the newest kept backup's instant and that last outcome” and rebuilt status “shows the newest kept backup's instant with the outcome `unknown`.”
open_points.question: What does the status contain and show when there is no kept backup, including after all old backups were deleted and the new run failed?
options: Use an explicit `no_backup` state with no instant
Show only the last failed-run outcome
Treat a missing newest-backup instant as a startup error
open_points.default_guess: Use an explicit `no_backup` state and retain the last run outcome separately.

open_points.subject: daily and post-import backup collision
open_points.text: The post-import backup is made even when the day has a backup, the ordinary backup “is still made at 03:00”, and “runs never overlap.”
open_points.question: If an import-triggered run and the 03:00 run become due together, which runs first, is the other queued, and must both still be produced?
options: Queue both and run them serially in a defined order
Coalesce them into one backup
Let whichever starts first run and defer the other until the next start or day
open_points.default_guess: Queue both, run the post-import backup first, then the ordinary daily backup.

open_points.subject: archiving an anonymised project
open_points.text: A05 accepts “archiving an archived project” unchanged, while an anonymised project has status `archived`; A04 says an action on an anonymised project states no revision but places “anonymised” among lifecycle checks that may fail.
open_points.question: Does archiving an anonymised project return it unchanged, or is it refused because it is anonymised?
options: Accept it as the archived no-op and require no revision
Refuse it as an action on an anonymised project
Require a revision even though the anonymised project retains none
open_points.default_guess: Accept it unchanged as the archived no-op, with no stated revision.

open_points.subject: repeating an import after restore under a changed artifact vocabulary
open_points.text: R0-89 says an import lost with a pre-import backup “may then be made again”, while A16/A22 refuse an import file containing a pointer whose type is no longer declared.
open_points.question: If the release has removed a type present in the retained export, must disaster recovery permit the repeated import, require the old release, or refuse it under the current vocabulary?
options: Repeat the import only under the release whose vocabulary originally accepted it
Permit recovery imports to retain formerly accepted types
Apply the current vocabulary and allow the repeated import to be refused
open_points.default_guess: Require the release that originally accepted the export, then migrate the restored store through later releases.
